bull.b: Faster recurring-revenue growth is improving the quality and predictability of Rekor’s business mix. A larger contracted revenue base can support better planning, higher customer retention and stronger margins, while reducing reliance on individually timed project sales over the next several quarters.

Sustained gross-margin expansion indicates that Rekor’s software, recurring offerings and product mix are gaining operating leverage. Higher margins create more capacity to fund sales, product development and customer support, and improve the company’s path toward durable profitability as revenue grows.

bull.t: Lower Operating Costs and EBITDA Path
bull.b: The sharply smaller adjusted EBITDA loss, combined with reduced operating expenses and additional planned savings, shows meaningful progress toward a more sustainable cost structure. If execution continues, the expected move to adjusted-EBITDA profitability could reduce funding needs and strengthen operating resilience.

bear.b: Rekor remains materially unprofitable even after recent improvement, so revenue and gross-margin gains have not yet translated into positive earnings. Continued losses can erode equity, limit internally funded investment and keep the business dependent on successful execution of its cost and growth plans.

Negative operating and free cash flow remain a fundamental constraint because the company is not yet funding operations from internally generated cash. Even with improved burn, continued outflows may require further cost reductions or external financing, limiting flexibility during slower sales periods.

Increased scrutiny of automatic license-plate recognition creates a structural challenge for Rekor’s government and commercial expansion. Data-retention, sharing and access requirements may lengthen procurement, raise compliance demands and delay conversion of the active pipeline into recurring revenue.
